Me: Eh… this article is kind of silly. Like, the idea is fine but the execution is a little…

There have of course been some hiccups. A flame war has already broken out on our social networking app between Mechs and Sarks. There is currently no policy in place to deal with hate speech or threats of mind rape and corporeal transmogrification, so right now we're just advising users to avoid that particular forum thread.

+1

+ show block
– hide block

Users should also be aware that the algorithm for flagging memetic hazards is not as of yet a hundred percent effective, so viewing is at your own risk. No one's posted anything dangerous so far, but someone from AWCY? posted a photo called 'Penguin is Kink-shaming you'. It's a porcelain, cartoon penguin with a completely neutral expression, and when you look it in the eyes you feel like it's condemning your sexual preferences. Some commenters called it homophobic or heteronormative, but it really isn't because it condemns everything equally. You can be vanilla cishet, you can be ace, it doesn't matter, this penguin is disgusted by what you like. That's the kind of thought-provoking anart I love seeing from the anomalous community!

+2

The solution we arrived at was a human spirit confined to a soul-trap. The easiest way for us to create such a soul-trap is through Retrocausal Quantum Resurrection. This method essentially uses entanglements and other quantum effects to bring a dead body back to life. This does, however, have the rather nasty side effect of retroactively binding a person's consciousness to their body for the duration of their death. They are excruciatingly aware of their decomposing bodies, but so long as they're aware of something they'll generate EVE for us to harvest.

We executed one of our batteries but arranged to resurrect her 144 years in the future. Evidently, we are successful, as the cadaver is outputting more EVE particles than it ever did while it was alive, with no observable deterioration of the body. We have now executed all of our batteries and placed them in cryogenic dewars. In 144 years we'll resurrect them, and then probably kill them again so we can get another 144 years out of them.

Which means we can now tell our subscribers than Dark Web is 100% powered by renewable energy. It really goes to show that good ethics is good business.

+1,000,000


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

I heard once that the SCP wiki has two modes: horrifying and hilarious. You combined them into one in this thing and its awesome!

Also, I notice we have the same headcanons as far as SCP-2718 is concerned. We both agree what O5-11 claims he experienced after death is really what happened to him. We also agree that SCP-2718 is ''not'' the fate of all humans and is more a O5-11 thing. I had headcanoned it more as being his personnel Hell he went to for all the terrible things he had to do as an O5 (110-Montauk) but this explanation works to. The worst part about this skip is that it feels like something humans (well, just some humans) would do if it was possible. Though SCP-2718's article notes it only works once per person so the dead souls should be free eventually.

item.content:encoded: Liked the end and found the body thoroughly entertaining. The soul-slave thing ties up the whole affair in a nice horror bow - while that seems to be becoming the norm for MC&D articles it didn't really detract from my overall appreciation of the whacky-ish tone that underscores the piece's darker moments. I'm not a particularly big fan of the execution; it seems almost cheat-y, taking this ridiculous concept (an app for anomalous people) and then having MC&D treat it as a legitimate business premise, with regulations and precautionary measures, etc., but in the end that's sufficiently dampened by the fact you make a decent case for their sponsorship of it. The fact that it's really just a data-hoarding scheme suits their characterization as corporate bastards very nicely.

item.content:encoded:
What Happens After is the scip you're thinking of, and it was the inspiration for this as well as the soul-traps in SCP-3440. I also briefly allude to Retrocausal Quantum Resurrection in Freaky Commodities II. It's a horrifying concept and I'm milking it dry.

Though the intent of 2718 was that this is what happens to everyone, you have to ignore or discredit all the other afterlife scips, which doesn't make sense to me. Instead, my headcanon is that O5-11's condition was a result of the specific method of resurrection used. It was stated to involve quantum effects, and therefore had a retrocausal effect on the subject.

item.title: ...I never said she didn't have a robot hand.
item.content:encoded:
To paraphrase IHP, I'd like to thank Randomini for letting me mangle his character to an unrecognizable degree.

Click here for a wall of text about canon
If nothing is canon, then everything is canon...

When I posted my first Iris Dark article a couple months ago, Wills and Ways hadn't been added to in a year and a half, and that was about a year and a half after the previous addition. I was reasonably sure it was dead. I knew I was reimagining Iris to an extent, but I thought that maybe there was enough open to interpretation for her to still be the Iris from W&W, and that Dread & Circuses could then be part of the Acidverse, as I have also incorporated the Utterly Bazaar pretty strongly into the story-line.

Though Randomini has been very gracious and not taken issue with me writing an alternative version of his character, he has also made it very clear that she is an alternate version, and that neither my portrayal of her nor the events she participates in are congruent with his continuity. Now that he has resumed writing Wills and Ways I feel a little awkward simultaneously writing about an alternate version of his character, but fortunately for me Randomini is okay with it.

I just want to make it clear to everyone that my Iris is a different Iris from Randomini's Iris. Since she's the Iris of Dread & Circuses, I shall call her Dread Iris. This also means that Dread & Circuses is now officially a separate canon from Acidverse. My Marshall (even though I avoided naming him, it was Amos Marshall who showed up in She Remembered Me) and my Carter (though he hasn't shown up yet) are mostly the same as W&W's, but Randomini has also said that my Darke is very different from his Darke.

Something similar to Wills and Ways still happened in Dread and Circuses, but there will be some point of clear divergence. I don't know what will happen to W&W Iris, but Dread Iris became Darke's proxy and apprentice while remaining his heir. Dread Iris was also definitely aware of her heritage prior to the assassination and had at least some previous interactions with Darke.

I will incorporate future developments in Wills and Ways as I see fit, and when Iris shows up again in Dread & Circuses I'll probably mention she has a robot hand.

Anyway, thanks to my beta readers Freemayne Modern_Erasmus Superblobby Ekronak not_a_seagull and SrGunk.
